name: momentum_decay_adaptive_5s
author: adapted from claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: Momentum decays at different rates depending on market conditions. By computing the half-life of momentum (how long it takes for an initial price impulse to lose half its effect, estimated via the AR(1) coefficient on 1-min returns), we adapt the holding period and exit strategy. When half-life is short (< 10 bars), momentum decays quickly — use tight targets, quick exits. When half-life is long (> 30 bars), momentum persists — use wide targets, trailing stops. The inefficiency exists because most momentum traders use fixed holding periods regardless of current momentum persistence. The half-life reveals whether to hold the full move or take quick profits.
mechanism: Market microstructure varies across volatility regimes. In low-vol regimes, mean-reversion dominates as market makers provide tight liquidity. In high-vol regimes, momentum persists as liquidity thins and stop-cascades amplify moves. Adapting the signal to the current regime captures the appropriate edge for prevailing conditions.

conditions: HL_Regime != MEDIUM (must be in a defined half-life regime)

exit.signal_exit: AR1_Coeff turns negative (momentum regime shifts to mean-reversion)

weaknesses: AR(1) coefficient estimated on 60 1-min returns is statistically noisy — the standard error of phi at n=60 is approximately 1/sqrt(60) ≈ 0.13, making the half-life estimate imprecise
Half-life formula assumes AR(1) is a good model for the returns process — in reality, intraday returns may follow GARCH or higher-order AR processes, making the simple AR(1) half-life misleading
MEDIUM regime (HL 10-30) is excluded, losing approximately 40% of potential trading opportunities; the boundary between regimes is arbitrary
prior_art: Momentum half-life concept from Ornstein-Uhlenbeck mean-reversion estimation; AR(1) models in Box & Jenkins; applied to pairs trading by Bertram (2010); intraday momentum decay less studied
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
